tasks.short: Minor repairs and a notice when service is major

steps.what: Look up the fault on a separate machine screen.
Make minor electrical and mechanical repairs on the machine.
Draft the major service request when the adjustment fails.
Notify supervisors by sending the major service request.

tasks.design: The setter still makes the minor electrical or mechanical repair at the machine. The machine control ({OTHER}) already shows the fault code, so a second lookup stops. When the fault needs a technician, the setter drafts the request in {DOCS} and sends that request from {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: The repair is at the machine, and only the setter can tell a minor adjustment from a fault that needs a technician.
tasks.enabler_now: The machine control already stores the fault code for that machine, so a second lookup adds nothing.
tasks.still_hard: A wrong call on a live machine can harm the setter or scrap the job.
tasks.human_edge: The setter's hands on the adjustment, and the call that the fault is beyond a minor repair.

ambition.what: Call for major service the same shift a minor adjustment does not hold.

tasks.altitude: The week is still spent on the machines. The setter gains nothing new except a fault code that is already on the control when they start the repair.

reach.role: First-Line Supervisors of Production and Operating Workers
reach.task: Schedule a technician from the major-service request.
reach.learn: Which faults the setter can adjust, and which need a technician the same shift.

evidence.claim: A machine control commonly shows a fault code for the current stop. Model knowledge.
Sending a maintenance request inside the plant is ordinary internal messaging. It is not, by itself, a score of the setter. Model knowledge.

assumptions: Means round to screens 1, documents 6, mail 2, and in person 91. The workbook prior of 0.1 is omitted.
The machine control stores fault code, machine id, and time. The producer is the control itself. If the display is blank, the setter reads it during the repair.
The minor repair and the wording of the request stay at full time. Only the separate lookup stops.
The send is to a supervisor inside the plant. No focal upkeep.
unknowns: Whether this plant's controls show a fault code without a separate login.
research_questions: Which faults does this cell treat as minor adjustments, and which always go to a technician?

already_counted.description: The setter re-reads the major-service request before sending it.

incremental.description: The supervisor already receives major-service requests. No new upkeep is added for them.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: High is a shift where the setter had been opening a second screen for a fault the control already showed. Low is a shift with no separate lookup. The repair and the notice stay at full time.

approvals.approved_version: major service request sent to the supervisor

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Instruct other workers in setup and operation

steps.what: Read the procedure other workers will use on the machine.
Instruct other workers in machine set-up and operation.
Send the operation notes to the other worker.

tasks.design: The setter still instructs the other worker at the machine. They read the setup procedure in {DOCS}, show the stops and the first cycle, then send the notes from {EMAIL}. The lesson stays at full time.
tasks.previous_blocker: Setup is shown on a live machine, and a wrong stop can harm the other worker.
tasks.enabler_now: The written procedure already exists. It does not replace the lesson at the machine.
tasks.still_hard: Seeing whether the other worker set the stops the way the setter just showed.
tasks.human_edge: The setter watching the other worker's first setup on that machine.

ambition.what: Correct a wrong setup before the other worker runs the first part.

tasks.altitude: The week still includes time at the machine with the other worker. The setter does not hand the lesson off.

reach.task: Set the stops and run the first cycle the way the setter showed.
reach.learn: Which checks the setter expects before the first part.

evidence.claim: Showing a machine setup to a coworker is in-person instruction. A mailbox note does not replace it. Model knowledge.
Notes of a setup shared inside the crew are internal work instructions. Model knowledge.

assumptions: Means round to documents 5, mail 2, and in person 93. The screen prior of 0.5 and the workbook prior of 0.1 stay at zero and are omitted.
The setup procedure names the machine, the job, the stops, and the tool. It already exists before the lesson. If it is missing, the setter shows the setup without it.
The lesson and the notes stay at full time. The other worker is inside the plant. No focal upkeep.
unknowns: Whether this cell keeps a written setup procedure for every job.
research_questions: Which setups in this cell are new to the helper, and which they have already run?

already_counted.description: The setter re-reads the procedure when this job differs from the last one.
The setter re-reads the notes before sending them.

incremental.description: The helper's practice time is their own work and is not new upkeep of this design.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The lesson at the machine, the procedure read, and the notes all stay at full time. Nothing in this task is shortened.

approvals.approved_version: setup notes sent after the lesson

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Record pressure, stroke, feed, and speed

steps.what: Read pressure readings, stroke lengths, and speeds at the machine.
Check pressure and speed on the machine control.
File the operational record of pressure, strokes, and speeds.
Stop the workbook once the operational record holds the readings.
Stop the mailbox copy once the operational record is filed.

tasks.design: The machine control ({OTHER}) already stores pressure, feed, and speed for the job. The setter still reads the stroke at the machine, checks those values, and commits the four readings on the {OPS_SYSTEM}. The workbook and the mailbox copy stop. The record names the machine and the job, not a score of the setter.
tasks.previous_blocker: Pressure, stroke, feed, and speed were copied by hand from the gauge into a workbook and a document.
tasks.enabler_now: The machine control already holds pressure, feed, and speed, so those three need not be typed again.
tasks.still_hard: Stroke length is often read by eye, and a wrong reading scraps the part.
tasks.human_edge: The setter matching the stroke to the part in front of them before the record is committed.

ambition.what: Hold the job the same hour a recorded speed does not match the job.

tasks.altitude: The setter still stands at the machine for the readings. They commit a shorter record, and they do not keep a second copy.

reach.role: Inspectors, Testers, Sorters, Samplers, and Weighers
reach.task: Use the filed pressure, stroke, feed, and speed when they check the part.
reach.learn: Which reading belongs to which dimension on this job.

evidence.claim: A machine control can hold pressure, feed, and speed for the running job and pass those values to an operations record. Model knowledge.
Dutch works-council consent is required when machine data tied to an operator login can be used to observe behaviour or performance. Other countries differ.

assumptions: Means round to screens 3, workbook 4, mail 1, documents 10, and in person 82.

The operations record stores machine, job, time, pressure, stroke length, feed rate, and speed. The control produces pressure, feed, and speed. The setter types the stroke. If a tag is missing, the setter types that value too.
The record is not a score of the setter and is not tied to a login used to judge their work. National consultation rules vary.
Reading the gauges stays at full time. The screen check and the commit drop only because three values are already on the control. No focal upkeep.
unknowns: Which of these machines expose pressure, feed, and speed, and which still need every value typed.
Whether stroke length is measured by eye on this cell.
research_questions: For this cell, which of the four readings already exists on the control without a new sensor?

already_counted.description: The setter compares the control values with the gauges.
The setter checks the stroke and the copied values before committing the record.

incremental.description: A controls technician keeps the map from the machine control tags to the operations record.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: High is a shift where pressure, feed, and speed were already on the control and the setter typed only the stroke. Low is a machine with no sensor, so every reading is still written by hand. The gauge reading stays at full time.

approvals.approved_version: filed operational record of pressure, stroke, feed, and speed

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write programs that cut metal and plastic

steps.what: Read the feed workbook before programs cut metal.
Write programs that cut metal and plastic materials.
Load the draft program on the machine control.
Prove the cut in metal or plastic before anyone repeats it.
Send the proved program that cuts the metal.

tasks.design: The tool library on the machine control ({OTHER}) holds the standard feed and speed, so the workbook stops. The setter still writes the program in {DOCS}, loads a draft for the trial, and proves the cut in metal or plastic. Only the proved program is sent from {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Feeds lived in a separate workbook, and the path was judged on the first cut.
tasks.enabler_now: The control's tool library can hold the standard feed and speed for a tool and a material.
tasks.still_hard: The contour, the offsets, and the first cut can scrap the part or harm the setter.
tasks.human_edge: The setter proving the program on the machine before anyone else runs it.

ambition.what: Reuse the proved program the next time the same part is cut.

tasks.altitude: The setter still writes the path and still proves the first cut. They stop keeping feeds in a separate workbook.

reach.task: Keep the standard cycles and the tool library the setter drafts from.
reach.learn: Which cuts in this cell are a standard cycle, and which need a new path.

evidence.claim: Machine controls keep a tool library of feed and speed for a tool and a material, and a person still proves a new program on the machine. Model knowledge.
A program file shared with operators inside the plant is an internal work instruction. Model knowledge.

assumptions: The raw means sum to 100.1, so they are scaled by 100/100.1 and then rounded to screens 5, workbook 2, mail 2, documents 17, and in person 74.
The tool library stores tool, material, feed, and speed. A tooling technician keeps it. If a tool is missing, the setter types the feed while drafting.
The load for the trial is not the released program, because the prove-out can still change the path. The send after the prove-out is the release, and it stays inside the plant.
Writing the program and proving the cut stay at full time. No focal upkeep.
unknowns: Whether this cell writes programs at the control or in a file that the control then loads.
Which tools already have a feed and speed in the library.
research_questions: For the parts this cell repeats, how often is the program new rather than a proved program from last time?

already_counted.description: The setter re-reads the proved program before sending it.

incremental.description: A tooling technician keeps the standard feed and speed for each tool and material in the control library.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: High is a job whose tool and material were already in the library, so the workbook was not opened. Low is a new tool, so the setter still looks up the feed. Writing the path and proving the cut stay at full time.

approvals.approved_version: proved program sent to the operators
